record.paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
record.original_question: What structural restrictions, classification results, or fibration theorems can be established for smooth projective varieties whose anti-canonical divisor −K_X is pseudo-effective? A first concrete direction is to study surjective morphisms φ: X → Y with pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical divisor −K_{X/Y} and determine how that positivity restricts the geometry of φ.

evidence.quote: Proposition 5.3. — What can we say for (smooth) projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor?
Toward the above problem, it seems to be the first step to consider a surjective morphism φ : X → Y with the pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical −KX/Y .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth complex projective variety, and let K_X denote its canonical divisor. Recall that an R-Cartier divisor D on X is called pseudo-effective if its numerical class lies in the closure of the cone generated by classes of effective R-divisors. Assume that the anti-canonical divisor −K_X is pseudo-effective.

(a) Establish structural restrictions and classification/fibration theorems for such X. In particular, determine the extent to which −K_X being pseudo-effective forces X to admit a canonical fibration (for instance, a maximal rationally connected fibration, an Albanese map, or a locally trivial / locally constant fibration) onto a base variety whose canonical class is trivial or otherwise constrained, and describe the geometry of the general fiber.

(b) As a first step toward (a), let φ : X → Y be a surjective morphism between smooth projective varieties such that the relative anti-canonical divisor −K_{X/Y} := −K_X + φ*K_Y is pseudo-effective. Determine how this positivity assumption restricts the geometry of φ: in particular, address whether φ must be (after a suitable base change or étale cover) a locally trivial / locally constant fibration with rationally connected fibers, what can be said about the singular fibers and the discriminant locus, and how the positivity of −K_{X/Y} controls the variation and the base Y.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is broadly open in the pseudo-effective setting, but significant partial results exist for the stronger hypothesis that −K_X (or −K_{X/Y}) is nef or strictly nef. In particular, structure theorems have been proved for projective klt pairs with nef anti-canonical divisor (Cao–Höring; Ejiri–Gongyo; and subsequent works), showing that after a finite quasi-étale cover X admits a locally constant rationally connected fibration onto a klt variety with numerically trivial canonical class. Relative versions for fibrations with strictly nef or nef relative anti-log canonical divisor have also been established. The general pseudo-effective case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Structure theorem for projective klt pairs with nef anti-canonical divisor
status_evidence.snippet: X admits a locally trivial rationally connected fibration onto a projective klt variety with numerically trivial canonical divisor (after a finite quasi-étale cover).
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural result under the stronger nef hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic fibre spaces with strictly nef relative anti-log canonical divisor
status_evidence.snippet: Fibration is a locally constant fibration with rationally connected fibres, and the base is canonically polarized hyperbolic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result on fibrations with strictly nef relative anti-canonical divisor.

status_evidence.title: Nef anti-canonical divisors and rationally connected fibrations
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical dimension of −K_X coincides with that on a general fiber of the MRC fibration.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial result for nef anti-canonical case.
